title: CollectiblesManager.cs
summary: Per-scene manager: tracks every CollectibleItem, shows the 'F to collect' prompt for whichever is nearest, and keeps the per-item counts that Quests read through GetItemCount.

notes.text: Auto-resolved by name ('Player') in Awake if not assigned.
Canvas the floating 'F to collect' prompt is parented under.
A convenient place to list which prefabs this scene's collectibles use; not read by the runtime logic itself.
Default prompt text; the live text adds the item's display name.

notes.match: readonly Dictionary<string, int> itemCounts = new Dictionary<string, int>();
notes.text: What the player has collected, by item ID. This is what Quests read — the old Bag panel no longer exists.
Total pickups this scene, for any HUD counter that wants it.
Quest.AreCollectiblesComplete() calls this with each required ID. Unknown or empty IDs return 0.
Falls back to a GameObject literally named "Player" if nothing was wired in the Inspector.
Falls back to the first Canvas in the scene for the prompt text.
Builds the on-screen prompt text object in code instead of requiring a pre-built prefab.
Uses the shared Comic Neue Bold font, matching the rest of the game's UI theme.
Scans the scene once for every CollectibleItem and registers itself as their manager.
Suppresses the pickup prompt while a conversation is active, an NPC is nearby, or the Quest Journal is open.
Finds whichever in-range collectible is closest to the player, or null.
Shows the specific item's display name in the prompt.
Same keyboard-OR-mobile pattern used across every interactable.
The item calls back into Collect(item) below.
Includes inactive objects, so items already collected (and hidden) stay tracked.
Each item is told who its manager is, so item.Collect() can route here.
Linear nearest-neighbour search over all tracked items — fine at this scale; also prunes any destroyed items it finds.
Called by CollectibleItem.Collect(): bumps the total and that item ID's count, then plays the shrink-away animation.
This one line is what makes a Quest's 'collect X' requirement turn true.
Length of the shrink-away animation, in seconds.
Disable the item's colliders immediately so it can't be collected twice mid-animation.
1 - (1-t)^3 is a standard 'ease-out cubic' — fast start, gentle settle at the end.
Shrinks the item to almost nothing.
Hidden, not destroyed, so it remains a real GameObject for quest and save logic.
